Limitation as to time, prescription, .

la:noun:praesul.gloss: a public dancer who dances in leaps
senses: a public dancer who dances in leaps
the leader of the Salii (ancient Roman priests of Mars)
la:noun:praesul.html:
praesul, sŭlis, comm.
praesilio
,
one who leaps or dances before others, a dancer in public, public dancer.
Lit. (class.), ; .—
In partic., the leader of the Salii, who annually leaped and danced through the city, bearing the ancilia: fuit in eo sacerdotio (Saliorum) et praesul et vates et magister,.—
Transf., in gen., a presider, president, director; a patron, protector, etc. (post-class.): agri praesul,: fori,: praesul creatus litteris,; : Angerona, diva praesul silentii,; : et Junone calent hic arae praesule semper,.

la:noun:praesagitio.html:
praesāgītĭo, ōnis, f.
praesagio
,
a presentiment, foreboding, the faculty of divining or presaging (class.; cf.: praedictio, divinatio, praesagium, praesensio): inest in animis praesagitio extrinsecus injecta, atque inclusa divinitus,: divina,: praesagitio dicta, quod praesagire est acute sentire. Unde sagae dictae anus, quae multa sciunt, et sagaces canes, qui ferarum cubilia praesentiunt, Paul. ex Müll.

la:adj:praestabilis.html:
praestābĭlis, e, adj.
2. praesto
,
preeminent, distinguished, excellent (class.; usually only of things concr. and abstr.): res magnitudine praestabiles,: praestabilis insignisque virtus,: ingenium atque lingua,: linguā ac facundiā praestabilis,: (Deus) praestabilis super malitiā,exalted,.—With inf.: Calchas praestabilis hariolari, i. e. hariolando,.— Comp.: dignitas praestabilior,: fuerat praestabilius,preferable, better,: nihil amicitiā praestabilius,: utrum huic rei publicae melius fuisse et praestabilius me civem nosci an te?more advantageous,: neque majus aliud, neque praestabilius invenies,.

la:verb:praestituo.html:
prae-stĭtŭo, ŭi, ūtum, 3, v. a.
statuo
,
to determine or appoint beforehand, to prescribe (class.; syn.: praefinio, praescribo): ei rei dies Haec praestituast proxuma,; : diem praestituit operi faciundo,: nobis tempus,: dies,.—With a rel.-clause: praetor numquam petitori praestituit, quā actione illum uti velit, : nullā praestitutā die,without any fixed term,; cf. .

la:verb:praetereo.gloss: to pass by or go by
senses: to pass by or go by
to disregard, neglect, omit or miss
la:verb:praetereo.html:
praetĕr-ĕo, īvi, and more freq. ĭi, ĭtum, īre (
fut. praeteriet, ; ; ), v. n. and a.
Neutr.
To go by or past, to pass by: si nemo hac praeteriit,: ut arbitri sint, qui praetereant per vias,: praeteriens modo,in passing by,: quasi praeteriens satisfaciam universis,; cf. : te praetereunte,.—Of impers. and abstract subjects: nec, quae praeteriit, iterum revocabitur unda nec quae praeteriit hora; redire potest,: nocte hac, quae praeteriit, proxima,.—So of time: biennium praeteriit cum ille cubitum nullum processerit,: tertius jam praeteriit annus, cum interim, etc.,.—
To be lost, disregarded, perish, pass away, pass without attention or fulfilment (late Lat.): aut unus apex non praeteribit de lege,: figura hujus mundi,; ; .—
Act., to go by or past, to pass by, overtake, pass a person or thing.
Lit.: praeterire pistrinum,: jam hunc non ausim praeterire,: hortos,: jam hos cursu, jam praeterit illos,: Maura Pudicitiae cum praeterit aram,.—Pass.: praeterita est virgo,.—Of inanim. subjects: ripas Flumina praetereunt,flow past their banks,.—
Trop.
To pass by an evil, to escape a danger: nescis, quid mali Praeterieris,.—
With neutr. adj., or a clause as subject, to escape one, i. e. to escape one's knowledge, be unknown to one: non me praeterit ... me longius prolapsum esse,: sed te non praeterit, quam sit difficile,: nec dubitamus multa esse, quae et nos praeterierint, praef. § 18.—
To pass by or over, i. e.
To pass over, leave out, omit, not mention: quae nunc ego omnia praetereo ac relinquo,: ut hoc praeteream, quod, etc.,, § 178: omitto jurisdictionem contra leges, caedes relinquo, libidines praetereo,: et quod paene praeterii, Bruti tui causā feci omnia,what I had nearly failed to mention,: aliquid silentio,: praeteream, referamne tuum ... Dedecus?: ut nihil praeteream,: ne quid praetereatur,.—
To pass over, omit, make no use of: locus, qui praeteritus neglegentiā est,.—
To pass over, to omit, leave out, in reading or writing, : litteras non modo, sed syllabas praeterit,.—
To neglect or forget to do a thing, to omit, leave out, in action; with inf.: verum, quod praeterii dicere, neque illa matrem, etc.,: quod sciscitari paene praeterivi,.—With acc.: nullum genus crudelitatis praeterire,to leave unpractised,.—Pass.: tantā vi dixisse ut nulla pars orationis silentio praeteriretur,left without applause,.—
In elections. legacies, invitations, donations, etc., to pass over, take no notice of, to neglect, reject, exclude any one: populus solet nonnumquam dignos praeterire: nec, si a populo praeteritus est, etc.,: cum sapiens et bonus vir suffragiis praeteritur,: Philippus et Marcellus praetereuntur,were passed by, received no appointment,: fratris filium praeteriit,has passed by, bequeathed nothing to,: me quoque Romani praeteriere patres,neglected me, forgot me,: quid repente factum, Quod sum praeteritus vetus sodalis?: si eum (filium) silentio praeterierit, inutiliter testabitur,.—
To go beyond, to surpass, excel: hos nobilitate Mago Carthaginiensis praeteriit,: virtus alios tua praeterit omnes,: ut Ajax praeteriit Telamonem,.—
To transgress: justum praeterit ira modum,due limits,. —Hence,
praetĕrĕunter, adv., in passing, cursorily (eccl. Lat.): loqui,, in Joann.—
praetĕrĭ-tus, a, um, P. a., gone by, past, past and gone, departed: nec praeteritum tempus unquam revertitur,: aetas,: anni,: nox, Prop 2, 11 (3, 6), 9: culpa,: labor,: secula,: vita,: viri,dead and gone, departed, (3, 5, 36): negotiantes veniā in praeteritum donavit,for the past, for their past conduct,: praeteritā noc. te,last night,.—In gram.: tempus praeteritum, the past or preterit tense: quaedam verba etiam mutantur, ut fero in praeterito,.—Subst.: prae-tĕrĭta, ōrum, n., things gone by, the past: sevocatus animus a contagione corporis meminit praeteritorum, praesentia cernit, futura praevidet,; : monet ut in reliquum tempus omnes suspiciones vitet: praeterita se fratri condonare dicit,: invidiam praeteritorum contemptu praesentium demere,.—Prov.: praeterita mutare non possumus, —In partic., Praetĕrĭta, ōrum, n., things passed over (Gr. παραλειπόμενα), a name of the books of Chronicles, because they contain what had been omitted in the books of Kings, , n. 1.

la:verb:praetermitto.gloss: to allow or permit to pass
senses: to allow or permit to pass
la:verb:praetermitto.html:
praeter-mitto, mīsi, missum, 3, v. a.
To allow or permit to go by, to let pass (class.; syn.: omitto, neglego).
In gen.: nullum diem,: nullam occasionem profectionis, Auct. B. Afr. 1: neminem,.—
In partic.
To omit, neglect, leave undone: nullum officium,: voluptates,: scelus,: praetermittendae defensionis plures solent esse causae,.—With inf.: reliqua quaerere praetermittit,: quod facere nullum diem praetermittebat,. —
In reading or writing, to pass over, leave out, make no mention of, omit: quod verba sint praetermissa,: si quid aut praetermissum aut relictum sit,; ; : officii praetermissi reprehensio,: nihil videmur debere praetermittere, quod, etc.,: quod dignum memoriā visum, praetermittendum non existimavimus,; ; . —
To pass by, overlook, wink at: do, praetermitto,overlook,: praetermittere et humanis concedere rebus, (by Lachm. written separately).—*
To let over, carry over, transmit, transport: an facili te praetermiserit unda Lucani rabida ora maris?.

la:prep:praeter.html:
praeter, adv. and prep.
prae, with the demonstrative suffix ter, as in inter, subter, propter
, signifies motion
by or past, and hence, also, beyond, or rest outside a thing.
Adv., past, by, beyond (cf. praeterquam), in the trop. sense; i. e.
Comparatively, before, beyond, above, more than (only ante-class.): quae praeter sapiet quam placet parentibus,: quod mihi videre Facere, et praeter quam res te adhortatur tua,.—
Exceptionally, except, excepting, unless, save (class. but rare): etiam e Graecis ipsis diligenter cavendae sunt quaedam familiaritates, praeter hominum perpaucorum,: ne quis praeter armatus violaretur, Weissenb. ad loc.: diem statuit, ante quam liceret sine fraude ab armis discedere, praeter rerum capitalium damnatis,: religionum usquequaque contemptor, praeter unius deae Syriae,; : exsules, praeter caedis damnati, restituebantur,

: praeter hodie,: nil praeter salices cassaque canna fuit,: uti pueri in curiam ne introeant, praeter ille unus Papirius,.—In connection with the particles si, quod, que: praeter si aliter nequeas,unless,: praeter quod epulis alienis voluptates meas anteferrem, etc.,besides that,: montes in Arcadiā Cyllene, Lycaeus ... praeterque ignobiles octo,and besides, and also,: praeterque,; ; ; 11, 4, 3, § 10. —For praeter quam and praeter propter, v. praeterquam and praeterpropter.—

Prep. with acc., past, by, before, in front of, along.
Lit., of place (rare but class.): mustela murem mihi abstulit praeter pedes,: magni montes solem succedere praeter,: praeter castra Caesaris suas copias transduxit,: servi ejus praeter oculos Lollii haec omnia ferebant,before the eyes of,: Ligures praeter oram Etrusci maris Neapolim transmisit,: praeter radices montis lapsus amnis,: praeter ora suorum,: tela volant ... Praeter utrumque latus praeterque et lumen et aures,: praeter majorum cineres rapitur Lateranus,.—
Trop.
In gen., over, beyond; against, contrary to, aside from: nihil praeter rem locuti sumus,beside the matter, irrelevant,: praeter aetatem stultus,: praeter aequom delinquere,: multa praeter spem evenisse,; cf.: quor sedebas in foro Tu solus praeter alios,apart from,: praeter naturam praeterque fatum,: praeter consuetudinem,: cum lacus Albanus praeter modum crevisset,: quod mihi videre praeter aetatem tuam Facere,.—
In partic.
Comparatively, of that which goes beyond something else, beyond, above, more than; esp.: praeter ceteros, alios, omnes, etc.: illud praeter alia mira miror,: praeter ceteros laborabis,; : quae me igitur res praeter ceteros impulit, ut, etc.,: necesse est quod mihi consuli praecipuum fuit praeter alios, id jam privato cum ceteris esse commune,: ut Argonautas praeter omnes candidum Medea mirata est ducem,; .—With neg.: nonne ostendis te vereri, quod praeter ceteros tu metuere non debeas,less than the rest,.—
Of that besides which there is something else in addition, besides, together with, in addition to: ut praeter se denos ad colloquium adducerent,: praeter imperatas pecunias,: ut praeter auctoritatem vires quoque haberet,: praeter illud commodum, quod, etc., tum etiam, etc.,.—
Exceptionally, besides, except: nec nobis praeter me alius est servos,: hoc nemini praeter me videtur,: omnibus sententiis praeter unam condemnatus est,: neque vestitus, praeter pelles habeant,: frumentum omne, praeter quod secum portaturi erant, comburunt,: nullas (litteras) acceperam praeter quae mihi binae redditae sunt, etc.,: ex plurimis honoribus, praeter paucos non recepit,.—
Praeter haec, for praeterea, besides that, besides, moreover (ante- and postclass.), ; .!*? In composition, praeter has the signification of past, by, and beyond, or besides; e. g. praeterducere, praetermittere, praeterea.

la:noun:praetor.html:
praetor, ōris, m.
for praeitor, from praeeo
.
Prop., a leader, head, chief, president: regio imperio duo sunto: iique praeeundo, judicando, consulendo, praetores, judices, consules appellantor,.—So, in gen., of the chief magistrates in colonies, as in Capua: cum in ceteris coloniis duoviri appellentur, hi se praetores appellari volebant,; cf. the context.—Of the Roman consul as chief judge, .—Of the dictator: praetor maximus,: aerarii, president of the treasury, an office created by Augustus, ; .—Of the suffetes in Carthage, .—Of generals, commanders of foreign nations, ; ; et saep.—
In partic., a prœtor, a Roman magistrate charged with the administration of justice; the office was first made distinct from the consulship A. U. C. 387. After the first Punic war, A. U. C. 490, there were two, praetor urbanus for Roman citizens, and praetor peregrinus for strangers, ; : praetor primus centuriis cunctis renunciatus, i. e. appointed first, ; ; Gai. lnst. 1, 6; 1, 78. The praetor had a tribunal where he sat on the sella curulis, with the judges on subsellia beside him. But he used to decide less important controversies wherever the parties found him: e plano,: in aequo quidem et plano loco,: Quid vis in jus me ire? tu's praetor mihi,.—
Transf.
For propraetor, a proprœtor, an officer who, after the administration of the prœtorship, was sent as governor to a province, ; —
For proconsul, q. v., ; .

la:adj:praetorius.html:
praetōrĭus, a, um, adj.
id.
.
Of or belonging to the prœtor or prœtors, prœtorian: jus,proceeding from the prœtor, consisting of his decisions,: comitia,the election of prœtor,: potestas,the office of a prœtor,: turba,to be found about the prœtor, accustomed to wait upon him,: jus praetorium, quod praetores introduxerunt adjuvandi, vel supplendi, vel corrigendi juris civilis gratiā: quod et honorarium dicitur,; : pignus,: tutor,a guardian appointed by the prœtor Urbanus,.—
Subst.: praetōrĭus, ii, m.
One who has been prœtor, an exprœtor, .—
One of prœtorian rank, .—
Of or belonging to the proprœtor, proprœtorian: domus deferebantur,his official residence in a province,: exercitus,.—
Of or belonging to a general: praetoria cohors, the cohort or body-guard attached to every general, a prœtorian cohort, ; cf.: praetoria cohors est dicta, quod a praetore non discedebat. Scipio enim Africanus primus fortissimum quemque delegit, qui ab eo in bello non discederent et cetero munere militiae vacarent et sesquiplex stipendium acciperent, Paul. ex Müll.—Hence, derisively: scortatorum cohors praetoria,.—The emperors especially had cohorts as a body-guard: castra,the camp of the prœtorians,; ; : cohortes navis,the flag-ship, the admiral's ship,: puppis,: imperium,the chief command,: porta, the gate of the camp that opened from before the general's tent directly towards the enemy (opp. the porta decumana, which was on the side farthest from the enemy), : praetoria porta in castris appellatur, quā exercitus in proelium educitur, quia initio praetores erant, qui nunc consules, et hi bella administrabant, quorum tabernaculum quoque dicebatur praetorium, Paul. ex Müll.

la:noun:praetorium.html:
praetōrĭum, ii, n.
praetor
.
A general's tent, : dictatoris,: imperatoris Aequorum,; .—
Transf.
A council of war (because held in the general's tent): praetorio dimisso,; : missum,.—
The official residence of the governor in a province, : curritur ad praetorium,, § 92; .—
A palace (post-Aug.): sedet ad praetoria regis,: Herodis,; .—
In gen., a magnificent building, a splendid country-seat (post-Aug.): ampla et operosa praetoria,: in exstructionibus praetoriorum atque villarum,; : alternas servant praetoria ripas,; ; ; .—
Of other dwelling - places, the cell of the queen-bee: et circa regem atque ipsa ad praetoria, densae Miscentur,. —Of Diogenes's tub: utcumque sol se inclinaverat, Diogenis simul praetorium vertebatur,.—
The imperial body - guard, the guards, whose commander was called praefectus praetorio or praetorii: in praetorium accepti,: meruit in praetorio Augusti centurio,: militare in praetorio,: ascriptis veteranis e praetorio,: praetorii praefectus,.

la:adv:praeterea.html:
praetĕr-ĕā, adv.
is
.
Beyond this or that, besides: si eum reddis mihi, praeterea unum nummum ne duis,: nihilne vobis in mentem venit, quod praeterea Crasso requiratis?: haec duo praeterea oppida,: auxiliis, equitatuque comparato, multisque praeterea viris fortibus Tolosā et Narbone evocatis,: quicquid praeterea navium habebat,; : si duo praeterea talis Idaea tulisset Terra viros,two more,: praeterea quam (rare for praeterquam): nihil praeterea cum consule pacti, quam quod, etc.,.—
Distributively in succession, besides, moreover: multae sunt causae ... primum ... praeterea,: primum ... tum praeterea ...,: quicumque bona patria laceraverat; quique alienum aes grande conflaverat; praeterea omnes undique parricidae; ad hoc quos, etc.; postremo omnes, quos, etc.,: nam et ... prudentiam mihi tuam exposuit: et praeterea suavitatem tuam adjunxit: praeterea summam erga se liberalitatem,: nunc ... praeterea ... tum porro,.—
In continuation, henceforth, hereafter; thenceforth, thereafter: et quisquam numen Junonis adorat Praeterea?: neque illum ... praeterea vidit,.

la:adv:praeterquam.html:
praeter-quam (separate, praeter enim quam, ; infra), adv.,
beyond, besides, except, save (class.): neque, praeterquam quas ipse amor molestias Habet, addas,: verbum si mihi unum, praeterquam quod to rogo, faxis, cave,: virgo quae praeter sapiet quam placet parentibus,: nullum praemium postulo, praeterquam hujus diei memoriam sempiternam,: interrogari, num quo crimine esset accusatus, praeterquam veneni ejus,: a quā (moneta), praeterquam de sue plenā, quid umquam moniti sumus?: si nullam praeterquam vitae nostrae jacturam fieri viderem,: sine ullis doloribus, praeterquam quos ex curatione capiebat,: nec quod nos ex conubio vestro petamus, quicquam est, praeterquam ut, etc.,: multitudo coalescere nullā re praeterquam legibus poterat,; ; ; 26, 42, 8: telum hastili abiegno et cetera tereti praeterquam ad extremum,: cuncta potest ... vetustas, Praeterquam curas attenuare meas,.—With etiam, quoque, tum vero, besides, = not only ... but also: malum, praeterquam atrox, etiam novum,; Weissenb. ad loc.; cf. : Syracusarum oppugnatio ad finem venit, praeterquam vi ac virtute ducis, intestinā etiam proditione adjuta,: lusit ... praeterquam Decembri mense, aliis quoque festis ac profestis diebus,: declamaverat Antonius praeterquam semper alias, tum vero nimium quantum delectabiliter,: praeterquam si, except when, unless: hippopotamus tergoris impenetrabilis, praeterquam si umore madeat,: praeterquam quod, except that: omnes mihi labores fuere leves, praeterquam tui carendum quod erat,: praeterquam quod sine te, ceterum satis commode, etc.,: praeterquam quod ita Quintio placeret,: amissio nullius animae, praeterquam navis,but ... only,.—With praeterea: praeter enim quam quod comitia illa essent armis gesta servilibus, praeterea, etc.,.—
For praeterquam quod, except that, .

la:noun:praetura.html:
praetūra, ae, f.
praetor
,
the dignity or office of a prœtor, the prœtorship (class.), : praeturae jurisdictio,: praeturā se abdicare,; .—
The term of office of a prœtor: intra ejusdem praeturam agere,; .

la:verb:praeterlabor.gloss: to slip, glide or flow by
senses: to slip, glide or flow by
la:verb:praeterlabor.html:
praeter-lābor, lapsus, 3,
v. dep. n. and a.
Lit., to glide or flow by, to fly or run past: praeterlabentia flumina,.—With acc.: tumulum,: hanc (tellurem) pelago praeterlabare necesse est,to sail past,.—
Trop., to slip away: (definitio) ante praeterlabitur, quam percepta est,.

la:verb:praetervehor.gloss: to drive, ride sail etc. by
senses: to drive, ride sail etc. by
la:verb:praetervehor.html:
praeter-vĕhor, vectus sum (separate, praeter erant vecti, ), 3,
v. dep. n. and a.; prop., to be borne past, to drive, ride, or sail by (class.).
Lit.: qui praetervehebantur,: praetervehens equo,riding by,.—With acc.: Apolloniam,: ostia,: Dulichios portus,: Judaeam,: Puteolanum sinum,: Velabrum,.—
Transf., to pass by, march by, of foot-soldiers: cito agmine forum praetervecti,.—
Trop., to pass by or over: periculosissimum locum silentio sum praetervectus,passed over in silence,: scopulos praetervecta videtur oratio mea,passed by,: oratio, quae non praetervecta sit aures vestras, sed, etc.,; .

la:verb:praetento.html:
prae-tento or praetempto, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
To feel, search, or grope out beforehand, to examine previously, to estimate beforehand, anticipate (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose): praetentare baculo, luminis orbus, iter,: praetentat manu silvas,: praetentat pollice chordas,: pedibus praetentat iter,: cochleae corniculis praetentant iter,: sinum,: culcitis et stragulis praetentatis et excussis,: fato pericula vestra praetentate meo,.—
Trop., to test or try beforehand: vires,: judicis misericordiam,.—
To hold before one's self: praetentat pallia laevā,.—
Trop., to make a pretext of: impia praetentans vulnera,.

senses: to place before or in front
la:verb:praetexo.html:
prae-texo, xŭi, xtum, 3, v. a.,
to weave before or in front, to fringe, edge, border.
Lit. (mostly poet.): purpura saepe tuos fulgens praetexit amictus,: glaucas comis praetexere frondes,weave around,; : praetexit arundine ripas Mincius,: litora curvae Praetexunt puppes,: fontem violis, Claud. Cons. Prob. et Olybr. 249: limina ramis, Rapt. Pros. 2, 320: ripam ulvis,: sicubi odoratas praetexit amaracus umbras,spreads over,.—In mid. force: utraeque nationes Rheno praetexuntur,border on the Rhine,.—
Transf.
To place before or in front (syn.: praetendo, praepono): in his voluminibus auctorum nomina praetexui, Plin. praef. § 21: auctores quos praetexuimus volumini huic,: tibi maximus honor excubare pro templis, postibusque praetexi,i. e. that your statues stand before the temples,.—
To border, to furnish, provide, or adorn with any thing: ex primo versu cujusque sententiae primis litteris illius sententiae carmen omne praetexitur, the whole poem is bordered (like an acrostic) with the initial letters from the first verse of every sentence (oracle), : omnia quae aguntur acerrime, lenioribus principiis natura praetexuit, has provided with, etc., : praetexta quercu domus,; : summaque praetexat tenuis fastigia chartae, Indicet ut nomen, littera facta, meum,let my name be inscribed upon it,.—
Trop.
To allege as an excuse, to pretend, to assign as a pretext (syn. causor): cupiditatem triumphi,: nomina speciosa,.—With acc. and inf.: ubicumque ipsi essent, praetexentes esse rempublicam,: Tigellinus T. Vinii potentia defensus, praetexentis, servatam ab eo filiam,.—
To cover, cloak, conceal, disguise with any thing: hoc praetexit nomine culpam,: funera sacris,: fraudem blando risu,.—Hence, praetextus, a, um, P. a., clothed with or wearing the toga praetexta: praetextus senatus (for praetextā in dutus),pubes,.—
In partic.
Toga praetexta, and (post-Aug.) absol.: praetexta, ae, f., the outer garment, bordered with purple, worn at Rome by the higher magistrates and by free-born children till they assumed the toga virilis, ; ; ; ; ; ; et saep.: praetextā pullā nulli alii licebat uti, quam ei, qui funus faciebat, Paul. ex Müll.—Hence,
praetexta, ae, f. (sc. fabula), a tragedy, because celebrated Romans (like Brutus, Decius, Marcellus) were represented in it: nostri vestigia Graeca Ausi deserere, et celebrare domestica facta, Vel qui praetextas vel qui docuere togatas,; Pollio ap. : praetextam legere,.—
praetextum, i, n.
An ornament, as something wrought or fastened in front (post - Aug.): pulcherrimum reipublicae praetextum,.—
A pretence,

prae-tendo, di, tum (

Lit.: praetenta Tela,stretched forth, presented,: propagines e vitibus altius praetentos, shooting forth, Fab. Pict. ap. : ubi visum in culice natura praetendit? set out, stationed (i. e. extendit, et posuit in anteriore oris parte), .—
Transf.
To spread before or in front: membrana, quae praecordia appellant, quia cordi praetenditur,; .—

Of places: praetendi, to stretch out before or in front of, to lie over against or opposite to (poet. and post - Aug.; once in Liv.): praetentaque Syrtibus arva,: tenue litus praetentum,: Armeniae praetentus Iber,: gens nostris provinciis late praetenta,: Baeticae latere septentrionali praetenditur Lusitania,: a tergo praetendantur Aethiopes, ; : Dardanis laevo Triballi praetenduntur,: extremis legio praetenta Britannis, i. e. opposita custodiae causa,.—

senses: to turn attention to, to attend to

prae-verto or -vorto, ti, 3, v. a., and (only in present tense) praevertor or -vortor (

Trop.
To be beforehand with, to anticipate; with acc., to prevent, make useless: nostra omnis lis est: pulcre praevortar viros, will anticipate, be beforehand with them (cf. praevenio), : aggerem et vineas egit, turresque admovit: quorum usum forte oblata opportunitas praevertit,has rendered useless,: praevertunt, inquit, me fata,prevent me,: celeri praevertit tristia leto,: quae absolvi, quoniam mors praeverterat, nequiverunt,.—
To take possession of beforehand, to preoccupy, prepossess: vivo tentat praevertere amore Jampridem resides animos,to prepossess,; cf.: neque praevorto poculum,take before my turn,.—
To surpass in worth, outweigh, exceed, to be preferable, of more importance: erilis praevertit metus,: quoniam pietatem amori tuo video praevortere, outweigh,

exceed, : nec posse, cum hostes prope ad portas essent, bello praevertisse quicquam,.—

To turn one's attention first or principally to, to do first or in preference to any thing else, to despatch first; used esp. in the dep.
With dat.: rei mandatae omnes sapientes primum praevorti decet,to apply themselves principally to it, to despatch it first,: ei rei primum praevorti volo,: stultitia est, cui bene esse licet, cum praevorti litibus,to occupy one's self with contentions,: cave, pigritiae praevorteris,do not give yourself up to indolence,: etsi ab hoste discedere detrimentosum esse existimabat, tamen huic rei praevertendum existimavit,.—

With an adverb of place: illuc praevertamur,let us first of all look at this,.—(ε) With a rel.-clause; proximum erat narrare glandiferas quoque, ni praeverti cogeret admiratio, quaenam esset vita sine arbore ullā, , praef. § 1.—(ζ) Absol.: in rem quod sit, praevortaris, potius quam, etc.,do, perform, attend to,.
